🇫🇷 Marine Le Pen’s victory in the French presidential elections could trigger the largest crisis in the history of the European Union. “France may refuse to recognize many EU laws and agreements, as well as deviate from the union’s common foreign policy line, in particular by drawing closer to Russia,” writes Financial Times columnist Martin Wolf. Due to a public debt of 116% of GDP and a budget deficit of 5.1% at the end of 2025, France may need assistance from the European Central Bank if investors withdraw, but such aid will only be provided if EU budget rules are observed. According to the author, this will force the future authorities to choose between strict spending cuts and the risk of the country leaving the bloc.
